reconcile.note: Henry keeps the Gershonite family headed by Libni distinct from the Merarite family headed by Mahli, so the shared name marks two different men.

discrepancy.note: Wellhausen treats the Chronicler's Levitical genealogies in 1 Chronicles 6 as artificially constructed, of which this Libni doubling is one instance.

quotes.text: By artificial genealogies of rather a rough and ready kind the three families of singers, Heman, Asaph, and Ethan are traced up (1Chronicles v1.. 1 seq.) to the old Levitical families of Kohath, Gershon, and Merari
quotes.attr: Julius Wellhausen (d. 1918), Prolegomena to the History of Israel (1885), on the Chronicler's artificial construction of the Levitical genealogies in 1 Chronicles 6.

sides.snippet: These are the names of the sons of Gershom: Libni and Shimei.
sides.verseText: These are the names of the sons of Gershom: Libni and Shimei.

sides.snippet: The sons of Merari: Mahli, Libni his son, Shimei his son, Uzzah his son
